home.title: Your connection, in one place.
home.description: View subscriptions, traffic, devices, access links, payments, referrals, and support.

commandMenu.title: Command menu
commandMenu.description: Jump to a page or change the appearance.
commandMenu.placeholder: Type a page or a command…

states.sessionErrorDescription: The API did not answer. Check that it is running and reachable.
states.forbidden: You do not have access to this page
states.forbiddenDescription: Your roles do not include the permission this page requires. Ask an owner if you need it.
states.unsavedChanges: You have unsaved changes. Leave this page and discard them?

home.description: This release delivers the panel shell, operator accounts, and the audit trail. Customer, finance, and catalog surfaces arrive in the next versions.
home.accessDescription: The roles you hold and the permissions they grant. The API enforces exactly this set.

cards.operatorsDescription: Review who can sign in, and suspend an account when someone leaves.
cards.auditDescription: Search every recorded authentication, authorization, and configuration action.
cards.securityDescription: Manage your password, two-factor authentication, and active sessions.

home.noDashboardDescription: The operations dashboard needs the system.read permission. Your roles do not include it.

login.title: Sign in
login.challengeDescription: Enter the code from your authenticator app.
login.codeHint: You can also use one of your recovery codes.

errors.locked: Too many failed attempts. Try again later.
errors.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.network: The API could not be reached.

setup.title: Create the first owner
setup.description: This installation has no operator account yet.
setup.tokenHint: The setup token was printed to the API log when it started. It can be used once.
setup.passwordHint: At least 12 characters. Length matters more than symbols.

operators.title: Operators
operators.description: Everyone who can sign in to this panel.
operators.emptyDescription: Only the owner account exists so far.

confirm.title: Suspend this operator?
confirm.description: They will be signed out everywhere immediately and will not be able to sign in again until reinstated.

toasts.lastOwner: The installation must keep at least one active owner.
toasts.statusFailed: The status could not be changed.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.description: Every authentication, authorization, and configuration action, newest first. The trail is append-only.
audit.emptyDescription: Actions will appear here as operators use the panel.
audit.noMatchesDescription: Try widening or clearing the filters.
audit.error: The audit log could not be loaded

security.title: Security
security.description: Your password, two-factor authentication, and the devices signed in to your account.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.description: A code from your authenticator app, required at every sign-in.
twoFactor.recommendDescription: This account controls customer data and money. A password alone is not enough.
twoFactor.scanHint: Add this secret to your authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.
twoFactor.disableWarning: Your account will be protected by a password alone. Confirm with your password.
twoFactor.recoveryDescription: These are shown once. Each can be used a single time if you lose your authenticator.

errors.disable: Two-factor could not be turned off.

password.title: Password
password.revokesOthers: This signs you out everywhere else.

errors.wrongCurrent: The current password is not correct.
errors.generic: The password could not be changed.

sessions.title: Active sessions
sessions.description: Where your account is currently signed in.
sessions.revokeFailed: The session could not be ended.

operations.errorDescription: The API did not answer. Retry, or check the service health.
operations.emptyDescription: Records appear here as soon as there are any.
operations.noMatchesDescription: No record matches the current filter.

dashboard.noRevenue: No settled orders in this window.
dashboard.revenueDefinition: Three separate figures. Provider money and wallet credit are not added together: wallet credit was already counted as revenue when the balance was funded.

definitions.customer.status.active: Customer records that are neither suspended nor deleted. Not the same as having a live subscription.
definitions.customer.status.suspended: Customer records an operator has suspended.
definitions.customer.status.deleted: Customer records marked deleted under the retention policy.
definitions.customer.created.window: Customer records created inside the reporting window.
definitions.entitlement.active: Entitlements marked active whose end instant is still in the future.
definitions.entitlement.limited: Entitlements in the limited state, typically past a traffic or device cap.
definitions.entitlement.lapsed: Entitlements still marked active or limited whose end instant has passed.
definitions.entitlement.renewal.window: Active entitlements ending inside the reporting window.
definitions.traffic.observed: The traffic counter Omniflow last observed from Remnawave. Remnawave is authoritative; this is a snapshot, not a total.
definitions.payment.succeeded.window: Payment intents that settled inside the reporting window.
definitions.payment.inflight: Payment intents currently pending, awaiting action, or processing.
definitions.payment.failed.window: Payment intents that failed inside the reporting window.
definitions.payment.stuck: Payment intents in flight and untouched for longer than any supported provider should take.
definitions.support.open: Support tickets in the open state.
definitions.support.stale: Open tickets with no message for a day or more.
definitions.job.failed: Fulfillment operations that exhausted their retries.
definitions.job.overdue: Queued fulfillment operations whose next attempt was due some time ago.
definitions.webhook.unprocessed.window: Provider callbacks received but not yet processed.
definitions.webhook.unverified.window: Provider callbacks whose signature did not verify.
definitions.drift.open: Unresolved differences between Omniflow and Remnawave.
definitions.drift.missing_remote: Entitlements whose Remnawave user no longer exists.
definitions.outbox.unpublished: Domain events the publisher has not yet drained.
definitions.outbox.oldest_age: Age of the oldest unpublished event. A large backlog of fresh events is healthy; one old event is not.

customers.title: Customers
customers.description: Search by an identifier you already hold, then work through the customer's subscriptions, orders, wallet, and risk history.
customers.notFoundDescription: No customer record matches that identifier.

filters.queryPlaceholder: Customer ID, Telegram ID, or Remnawave username

actions.reasonPlaceholder: Why this change is being made
actions.notProvisioned: This subscription has no entitlement yet, so there is nothing to change. It is provisioned when a paid order is fulfilled.
actions.queued: Queued {operation}. The fulfillment worker applies it and records the result under System.

empty.riskDescription: No blocklist source lists any identifier for this customer.

devices.title: Devices
devices.unavailable: Devices are unavailable — Remnawave did not answer.

referrals.noInvitees: This customer has not invited anybody.
referrals.privacy: Invitees are identified only by their Omniflow identifier and whether they bought anything. Their account details are not part of this view.

timeline.emptyDescription: Operator actions against this customer appear here.

finance.title: Finance
finance.description: Order history, the reconciliation queue, and automatic charges that did not go through.

empty.stuckDescription: Every payment in flight is still inside the expected window.
empty.chargesDescription: Every automatic renewal in the recent history went through.

finance.chargesNote: A failed charge retries on a bounded schedule and then hands the customer back to manual renewal. Nothing here re-triggers one.

detail.description: Every payment attempt and refund against this order.
detail.noIntents: No payment was attempted for this order.
detail.refundReasonPlaceholder: Why this refund is being issued
detail.minorUnitsHint: The amount is an integer in the currency's minor unit. The payment service executes the refund against whatever the provider actually supports.

risk.title: Risk
risk.description: Blocklist matches and anomaly signals, with the evidence that produced them.
risk.noAutoAction: Nothing on this page changes a customer. A decision here records a verdict and a reason; suspending an account is a separate action on the customer's own page.

empty.matchesDescription: No blocklist match is waiting for a decision.
empty.anomaliesDescription: No metric has crossed its configured threshold.
empty.sourcesDescription: Add a source to check customer identifiers against a published list.

rules.explainer: A metric with no rule is not evaluated at all. Thresholds are in each metric's own unit, and a condition that persists raises one signal per window rather than one per sweep.
rules.incoherent: The alert threshold must be at least the warning threshold, and the window at least five minutes. A rule that fails this is skipped at evaluation time.

units.purchase: Paid order value per customer, in the currency's minor unit.
units.refund: Refunded value per customer, in the currency's minor unit.
units.referral: Qualified referrals per inviter, as a count.
units.traffic: Observed usage per subscription, in bytes. Remnawave owns traffic, so this is a level check rather than a rate.

sources.httpsOnly: HTTPS only. Over plain HTTP anyone on the path could decide who this installation refuses to serve.

system.title: System
system.description: Fulfillment jobs, provider callbacks, Remnawave drift, and the outbox backlog.

empty.jobsDescription: Every fulfillment operation has succeeded or is still retrying.
empty.driftDescription: Omniflow and Remnawave agree on every entitlement.
empty.outboxDescription: Every domain event has been published.

health.dependenciesDescription: The same probes the readiness endpoint reports on, so the panel and your load balancer can never disagree about whether a dependency is up.
health.providersDescription: What each configured provider last reported. "Configured but never reached" is a different problem from "reached and failing", so they are shown separately from the live probes above.
health.maintenanceDescription: Blocks new purchases and defers fulfillment. It never cancels, refunds, or expires anything already paid for.
health.reasonPlaceholder: Why maintenance is being engaged or cleared
health.noticesRequired: Both languages are required. A customer who reads only one and gets a blank screen is worse served than one who gets a notice they can read.
health.automaticNote: This was engaged by dependency detection, not by an operator. It clears itself when the dependency recovers; clearing it by hand would re-enable purchases while the dependency is still down.

catalog.title: Catalog
catalog.description: Plans, their versions, and the promotions that discount them.

empty.plansDescription: Create a plan before opening the catalog to customers.

version.title: Publish the next version
version.description: A plan version is immutable once an order references it, so this publishes a new one instead of changing the current one.
version.graceHint: Access continues this long after expiry. Zero disables it.
version.trafficHint: Leave empty for unlimited. Zero is not the same thing.
version.maxSquadsHint: Leave empty for no upper bound.

downgradePolicyValue.at_expiry: At the end of the period

cancellationPolicyValue.at_expiry: At the end of the period

version.pricesHint: Comma-separated CURRENCY=amount, in the currency's minor unit. For example RUB=49900, USD=599.
version.reasonHint: Why this version is being published.
version.immutability: Existing orders keep the version they were bought at. Publishing does not change any price a customer has already paid.

empty.title: No add-ons
empty.description: Add-ons let a customer buy extra traffic, device slots, or squads on top of a plan.

composer.title: Create an add-on
composer.description: The add-on row carries presentation and stays editable; the version carries what the customer gets and what it costs, and does not.

payloadHint.devices: Added to the subscription's device limit.

composer.quantityHint: How many of this add-on one order may include.
composer.pricesHint: Comma-separated CURRENCY=amount, in the currency's minor unit.
composer.immutability: Both languages are required. Saving publishes a new version; orders already placed keep the version they were bought at.

shop.title: Digital goods
shop.description: Telegram Premium and Stars sold alongside subscriptions. Nothing here touches a VPN entitlement.

empty.productsDescription: Add a product and a pricing rule before opening the shop.
empty.providersDescription: Configure a digital-goods provider to sell Premium or Stars.
empty.reviewDescription: No delivery is waiting on a human decision.

pricing.noPublishedCost: This provider publishes no cost for Telegram Premium, so the price must be fixed. The margin on such an order is recorded as unknown rather than as the whole price.
pricing.minorUnitsHint: Amounts are integers in the currency's minor unit. 1500 basis points is a 15% markup, and every rounding mode rounds up.

shop.reviewExplainer: The gateway honours no idempotency key, so a lost answer means the goods may or may not have been sent. Check with the provider, then record what you found — confirming delivery completes the order, and refunding credits the customer's wallet.
shop.reviewReasonPlaceholder: What you confirmed with the provider (required)

gifts.title: Gifts
gifts.description: Subscriptions, add-ons, and wallet credit bought for somebody else.

settings.title: Commerce settings
settings.description: Wallet top-up limits, subscription concurrency, and payment-provider status.
settings.unsavedChanges: You have unsaved changes. Leave this page anyway?

topUp.title: Wallet top-up
topUp.description: Limits are integers in the currency's minor unit.
topUp.presetsHint: Comma-separated minor units. Free entry stays available whatever this list contains.

subscriptions.title: Concurrent subscriptions
subscriptions.description: The installation-wide ceiling. A plan may narrow it further, never widen it.
subscriptions.multiEnabled: Allow more than one subscription per customer
subscriptions.disableNote: Turning this off closes nothing. Customers who already hold several keep them; the ceiling applies to new purchases.

providers.title: Payment providers
providers.description: What the operator configured, beside what each compiled-in adapter actually declares.
providers.recurringUnsupported: Adapter cannot store a payment method
providers.webhookHint: Secret used to verify inbound callbacks
providers.keepStored: Leave blank to keep the stored secret
providers.secretNotice: Stored secrets are sealed with the deployment's data encryption key and are never sent back to the browser. Leaving a field blank keeps what is stored.
providers.testExplains: The test performs an authenticated read; it never creates a payment.

probeError.timeout: The provider did not answer in time
probeError.unreachable: The provider could not be reached

providers.recurringUnsupportedLong: This integration has no way to bind a payment method, so automatic charging cannot be enabled for it.
providers.recurringExplains: Whether a merchant account may charge a saved method is granted by the provider and cannot be discovered. Record the outcome of your own test; automatic charging cannot be enabled without a passing one.
providers.recurringReasonPlaceholder: What was tested, and with which merchant account

offers.title: Personal offers
offers.description: A promotion pointed at one customer, with its own copy, validity window, and single redemption.

empty.title: No offers
empty.description: Targeted offers appear here once you create one.

composer.title: Create a personal offer
composer.description: The discount comes from an existing promotion, so the stacking rules and rejection reasons that already govern promotions govern this too.
composer.customerHint: The Omniflow identifier of the customer this is for
composer.reasonHint: Why this customer is being offered this
composer.singleUse: Both languages are required: an offer with copy in one language renders as a blank card for half your customers. The offer is redeemable once and is resolved the moment it is used, dismissed, or expires.

preview.title: What the customer will see
preview.approximation: An approximation of the Telegram message, not a live render — the bot draws the real one.

empty.title: No bulk actions
empty.description: Bulk actions you preview appear here with their per-item results.

composer.title: Preview a bulk action
composer.description: Previewing records the action and every target without applying anything. Nothing changes until you apply it.
composer.reasonHint: Why this is being applied to all of them
composer.previewNotice: Each target is applied and recorded one at a time, so a run that half succeeds says which half. Every change goes through the same fulfillment pipeline a single change uses.

imports.title: Import and export
imports.description: Customer imports are previewed before they are applied. A record that collides with somebody who already exists is counted as a conflict rather than silently merged or skipped.
imports.exportNotice: The export carries identifiers, status, locale, timezone, and counts. It deliberately carries no subscription link, payment token, or hardware identifier — an export is a file that leaves the installation.

empty.title: No imports yet
empty.description: Import runs and their validation results appear here.

support.title: Support desk
support.description: What is waiting, who has it, and how close it is to what the queue promised.
support.selectTicket: Choose a ticket to read it.
support.cannedHint: Only replies your role may send are listed.
support.sendHint: The bot delivers it, applying the customer's delivery preferences.
support.notePlaceholder: An internal note — the customer never sees this

aiSettings.title: AI and MCP
aiSettings.description: Providers, per-feature enablement, spend limits, and connected MCP servers. Nothing here runs until you turn it on.

providers.title: Providers
providers.description: What a provider does with the data you send is recorded here, from its own terms. Omniflow cannot verify these answers and does not try to.
providers.empty: No provider is configured, so every AI feature is unavailable.
providers.apiKeyPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current key

features.title: Features
features.description: Each feature is off until you enable it and choose a provider and model. Retention is set per feature, because a marketing draft and a support summary are not the same material.

warnings.provider_trains_on_data: This provider may train on your data

limits.title: Usage limits
limits.description: Ceilings by operator, role, feature, or installation. The narrowest applicable one is the one an operator is told about, because the remedy differs.

usage.title: Spend and performance
usage.description: Requests, tokens, latency, and estimated cost.
usage.window: {since} to {until}. No prompt or output content is stored, so none appears here.
usage.empty: No AI requests in this period.

mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.description: An MCP server is a third party your assistant can reach. A connection is off until you enable it, and reaches only the tools you allowlist.
mcp.limits: Timeout {timeout} · at most {calls} calls per request · depth {depth} · {bytes} per response
mcp.schemaUnusable: This build cannot enforce the declared schema, so the tool cannot be enabled.

mcpAudit.title: MCP activity
mcpAudit.description: Every call and every refusal. A trail that only records what happened cannot answer whether anyone tried.

marketing.title: Marketing
marketing.description: Campaigns, audience segments, the suppression list, and the referral programme.

campaigns.title: Campaigns
campaigns.description: A campaign is created in draft with its estimated audience already visible. Scheduling is a separate action.
campaigns.name: Name

segments.title: Audience segments
segments.description: Each definition is shown in words, generated from the filters themselves, so it cannot describe something the query does not do.

suppressions.title: Suppression list
suppressions.description: Customers who receive no marketing messages. Transactional messages are unaffected.

referrals.title: Referral programme
referrals.description: What an invite earns, who it earns for, and how long an invite stays attributable.
referrals.payless: Enabling a programme with no reward on either side sends the invites and pays neither party. Set a reward, or leave the programme off.

installationSettings.conflict: This screen is showing an older version of the section. Reload to see the current values before saving again — saving now would discard the other change.
installationSettings.secretPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the current value
installationSettings.secretsNote: Secrets are never returned after they are written. A field shown as configured holds a value this screen cannot display, and leaving it empty keeps it.

branding.title: Branding and contact
branding.description: The name, contact, and URLs customers see.

remnawave.title: Remnawave connection
remnawave.description: Where the panel reaches Remnawave, how often it reconciles, and the token it uses.

telegram.title: Telegram bot
telegram.description: Bot identity, webhook delivery, and the credentials behind them.

operatorGroup.title: Operator group
operatorGroup.description: Where operator notifications go, and how many arrive before they are collapsed.

requiredChannels.title: Required channels
requiredChannels.description: How often membership is re-verified and how long a customer has to rejoin before access is affected.

maintenance.title: Maintenance mode
maintenance.description: When maintenance turns itself on, and what customers are told while it is.

notifications.title: Notification thresholds
notifications.description: How bad something has to get before an operator is told, and when not to tell them.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.description: Whether anonymous version data leaves this installation, and where it goes.

backup.title: Backups
backup.description: Schedule, retention, and the key backups are encrypted with.

security.title: Sessions and security
security.description: How long an operator session lasts and what is required to start one.

telemetryPreview.title: What telemetry would send
telemetryPreview.description: The exact payload, rendered from the same values the sender uses. Nothing here identifies your customers, your revenue, or your domain.

backups.title: Backups and restores
backups.description: A backup nobody has ever restored is a backup nobody knows works, so the restore history sits here too.
backups.noRestores: No restore has ever been performed or tested.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics bundle
diagnostics.description: Version, schema state, configuration status, and counts — assembled from an allowlist, so it contains no secrets and no customer data.
